claims.text: Pre-heating the LPBF build platform to 500°C will reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi components relative to a non-heated platform.
Pre-heating the build platform to 500°C will improve the mechanical properties of LPBF AlCrFeNiSi components.
Build-platform pre-heating will simplify LPBF processing compared with conventional LPBF using a non-heated platform.
Pre-heating reduces the temperature differential between the molten pool and surrounding material.
Reducing the molten-pool temperature differential minimizes thermal gradients during solidification.
Lower thermal gradients reduce associated residual stresses.
Build-platform pre-heating promotes a more uniform microstructure.
A more uniform microstructure leads to improved mechanical properties.
Residual stresses will decrease by at least 30% relative to components produced on a non-heated platform.
Tensile strength will improve by at least 20% relative to components produced on a non-heated platform.
Ductility will improve by at least 20% relative to components produced on a non-heated platform.
The proposed processing window is 500°C platform temperature, 200 W laser power, 1000 mm/s scan speed, and 30 µm layer thickness.
The hypothesis applies to AlCrFeNiSi components with dimensions up to 10 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm.
Mechanical testing and residual-stress analysis are to be performed at room temperature.
Conventional LPBF with a non-heated platform produces higher residual stresses and lower mechanical properties.
Variations in powder quality, laser parameters, and build geometry may alter the magnitude of residual-stress reduction and mechanical-property improvement.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 30% residual-stress reduction and at least 20% improvements in tensile strength and ductility, but falsification is triggered only below 10%. Results between 10% and the predicted minima would violate the quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
